checks.name: mypy --strict
checks.output_tail: Success: no issues found in 101 source files

findings.title: Byte ceiling measured in characters, not bytes
findings.detail: max_bytes is compared against len(text) (characters) and the slice text[:max_bytes] cuts characters, so a diff of multi-byte UTF-8 can exceed the stated byte ceiling (up to ~4x) and the prompt budget is not actually enforced in bytes. The name and docstring promise bytes.

findings.title: Anchor compares model path against diff paths without normalisation
findings.detail: diff.paths holds paths after _safe_path stripping and prefix removal, but proposal.file is used verbatim. A model citing './src/x.py' or a path with a trailing space resolves to the same file via _resolve yet fails this membership check and is marked unverified, so a correct finding is silently downgraded. The check should compare resolved paths, not raw strings.

findings.title: Anchor reads the working tree, not the diff's new-file content
findings.detail: The quote is checked against the file on disk, while the model was shown the diff. For a deleted file (status 'deleted', path still in diff.paths) read_text fails and every finding becomes 'file does not exist'; for a modified file the on-disk line numbers may differ from the diff's new-file numbering if the working tree has moved on. The anchor should verify against the DiffLine text the model actually saw.

findings.title: No test evidence for anchoring and severity rules in the change
findings.detail: The change introduces anchor(), _severity(), _parse() and parse_diff() with non-trivial rules (blocking downgrade for non-defects, quote-elsewhere detection, fence stripping, path traversal refusal) but no tests are part of the diff; per project rules each new behaviour needs a test.

location.quote: anchor(index + 1, proposal, root, diff) for index, proposal in enumerate(proposed.findings)
